text:
Ryan Strome has quietly been one of Calgary's better forwards since coming over from Anaheim. RotoWire noted six points in his last six games, and he scored the opener against Chicago on Saturday. He has 12 points in 24 games at about 14 minutes a night, his goals right in line with his chances, and Calgary takes 51% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), about four points better than without him.

That matters on a team at 46% overall. He came over after 276 games in Anaheim, and his game has a clear shape in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: lots of shot attempts, many from outside the slot, and only 31% of entries carried in, so his line plays dump and chase. The fifth overall pick of 2011 has turned into a useful depth center. Our range has him around 41 points.
